labels.running:
Healthy induction
Choose another scenario
A fit 40-year-old man for elective surgery, preoxygenated with FiO₂ 1.0 by face mask: the oxygen stays on until you press “Induce now” (at 3:00 or later) and the mask comes off once the breathing has stopped. Watch the pressure fall after propofol and rocuronium and the breathing stop, then secure the airway. If nobody does, the case runs on: SpO₂ below 90 % about 8 minutes after induction, hypoxic bradycardia a minute later, the first tiny diaphragmatic efforts at about 15 minutes, too small to ventilate, and asystole at about 20 minutes. Ventilate at any point before the arrest to rescue him: asystole after prolonged hypoxia is rarely recoverable; ventilate before this point.
